title: I Used the Paper-Marbling Tray Hours on the Intern Who Left My Size Skin

parts.text: I skimmed tray three at 10:08 a.m. and intern Noor was already dropping on my numbered size. The card said: ONE TRAY. FORTY MINUTES. SIZE STAYS WITH THE BOOKING. I was thirty-two, paper studio member, holding a comb that listed our pattern. Noor shrugged. "Interns are the tray." I photographed the card, the booking, and her rake on my skin. Then I asked for the tray log. At 10:16 the studio pinged why Noor's name was on my size. I kept my voice studio-soft and let the timestamp talk. A card is only a card until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The studio can see Noor's rake on my skin during our booking.

social.video_title: She dropped on my numbered size and left the skin — Part 1/2
social.description: Marbling tray, an intern on my skin, a forty-minute card she posted. I logged the rake. Would you have asked for the tray log?

parts.text: Noor called it a test drop until the studio asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the card, and the rake still. The size went back to my tray. Noor ran her own forty and told the next intern atmosphere was always about stone. Stone is a word interns use when a booking exists. Tray policy now has a second line: INTERNS ARE NOT THE TRAY. I keep our comb on a labeled hook. Noor brown-bags her jokes. The studio finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Interns are not the tray — Part 2/2
social.description: Tray log, numbered size, and a second line on the card. Was a test drop ever my skin?
